item.title: Google Dodged an Ad-Tech Breakup — But Its Advertising Rules Are About to Change | Nightcap
item.description: Google escaped a forced breakup of its ad-tech business, but a federal judge ordered changes designed to open its advertising markets to more competition. Plus: the Federal Reserve raised rates for the first time since 2023, the SEC proposed a major shift in shareholder-vote oversight, and Dallas is becoming a proving ground for a cheaper drone-delivery model. Follow this podcast and @socialwithrob on Instagram for more marketing secrets.

item.title: The Fed Just Made Attention More Expensive | Evening
item.description: The Federal Reserve raises rates for the first time since 2023, OpenAI pushes sponsored agents deeper into ChatGPT, the SEC proposes a major shift in shareholder-vote oversight, and Google makes its biggest carbon-removal deal yet. Puck and Kore decode what higher capital costs, conversational commerce, corporate accountability and AI infrastructure mean for marketers. item.title: Ads Just Learned How to Talk Back
item.description: OpenAI is testing business-sponsored AI agents, AI adoption is racing ahead of obvious productivity gains, and forecasts for autonomous agents are getting enormous. Puck and Kore break down what conversational advertising could change, why marketers need better measurement instead of more AI theater, and why trust, taste, judgment and machine-readable brand truth may become more valuable as execution gets cheaper. Follow this podcast and @socialwithrob on Instagram for more marketing secrets.
